items.detail: US stocks turned higher Friday, capping a banner week: the **S&P 500 rose 0.3%**, the **Nasdaq climbed 0.9%** and the **Dow added 67 points (0.1%)** after a shock July jobs report.
items.why: Wall Street read the surprise drop in payrolls as raising the odds the Fed holds rather than hikes, reviving the easing hopes that underpin the rally.

items.detail: The rally paused Thursday: the **S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,723.55** and the **Nasdaq snapped a four-day win streak**, though the **Dow bucked the trend to a fresh record 54,349.12** (+263 points).
items.why: Oil rebounded to about $83 a barrel and Treasury yields rose after Iran's parliament was reported to be reviewing a bill barring 'hostile' vessels from the Strait of Hormuz, pressuring high-growth tech valuations.

items.detail: The July jobs report stunned to the downside: the economy **shed 23,000 payrolls** — its first drop in months, versus about **+83,000 expected** — while the **unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%** and wage growth slowed to **3.2%, the lowest since May 2021**.
items.why: Losses were concentrated in local-government education (-50,000) and retail trade (-19,000), pointing to a genuinely cooling labor market rather than a one-off.

items.detail: Rate expectations flipped hard: futures that on Thursday leaned toward a **September Fed hike** swung to pricing a **hold** after the payrolls miss.
items.why: The unexpected job losses undercut the case for further tightening, shifting the market's base case back to steady policy at the September 16 FOMC.

items.detail: Indian equities snapped their advance Friday: the **Nifty 50 fell 0.27% to 24,570.65** and the **Sensex dropped 0.58% to 78,499.17**, with private banks and financials the biggest drag.
items.why: Weak global cues and the rebound in crude back toward $83 soured sentiment, while heavy selling in private-bank names outweighed the rest of the market.

items.detail: Autos and IT cushioned the fall, with the **Nifty Auto index up 1.84%** and IT names offering support against the financials-led weakness.
items.why: Rotation into autos and export-oriented IT offset the private-bank selloff, keeping the headline index losses shallow.

items.detail: Despite Friday's dip, both benchmarks ended the week **up roughly 1%**, extending their winning streak to a **second consecutive week**.
items.why: Steady foreign inflows and easing inflation worries earlier in the week kept the broader uptrend intact even as Friday gave back some ground.

items.detail: Foreign buying is now the structural support: FIIs have purchased a **net $1.3 billion of Indian equities so far in August**, following **$2.1 billion in July**.
items.why: Sustained overseas appetite, drawn by firmer global risk sentiment and India's improving inflation backdrop, has underwritten the recent recovery.

items.detail: Crypto rallied on the US jobs data: **Bitcoin climbed to about $65,144** (from a $64,260 open) and **Ether rose to roughly $1,929** by Friday morning.
items.why: The weak July payrolls report boosted expectations that the Fed holds rather than hikes, pushing money back into risk assets including crypto.

items.detail: The ETF thaw is accelerating: US spot **Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $128.69 million** and **Ether ETFs drew $92.15 million** on Aug 6, with **BTC funds taking in over $750 million this week**.
items.why: A steady return of institutional demand after months of outflows is providing consistent price support beneath the recovery.

items.detail: The CLARITY Act is now formally sidelined: the **Senate left for its recess without a floor vote**, with the chamber in a state work period from **Aug 10 to Sept 11** and Majority Leader Thune saying the bill will be queued on return.
items.why: With no vote before the break, the near-term federal crypto framework is off the table until September, though Polymarket odds of 2026 passage edged up to about 31%.

items.detail: With the legislative catalyst deferred, macro is firmly in the driver's seat, leaving **Fed rate expectations and incoming data** — not crypto-specific news — as the swing factor for BTC and ETH.
items.why: The absence of a near-term regulatory catalyst means direction hinges on the same jobs-and-rates narrative moving equities.

crossCuttingTheme: The July jobs report replaced oil as the master switch: a surprise 23,000-job loss flipped Fed expectations from a September hike to a hold, lifting US stocks and crypto together on Friday — even as an oil rebound to $83 on a fresh Iran Strait of Hormuz threat had reintroduced the yield-and-inflation risk that clipped the S&P 500 and Indian financials a day earlier.
